description: STRENGTHENING RHODE ISLAND PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE, AND DATA SYSTEMS - THE RHODE ISLAND DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (RIDOH) SEEKS $11,857,193 IN SUPPORT FOR YEAR 1 FROM THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL UNDER CDC-RFA-OE22-2203 TO ADDRESS CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDS TO BETTER MEET THE NEEDS OF THE 1,095,610 RHODE ISLAND RESIDENTS THAT MAKE UP THE TARGET POPULATION. RIDOH SEEKS FUNDING UNDER COMPONENT A, STRATEGY A1: WORKFORCE, STRATEGY A2: FOUNDATIONAL CAPABILITIES, AND STRATEGY A3: DATA MODERNIZATION.  THE PURPOSE OF THE WORK UNDER STRATEGY A1 (WORKFORCE) IS BOLSTER THE EXISTING WORKFORCE AND TO ATTRACT AND RETAIN DIVERSE NEW HIRES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE HIRING A WORKFORCE DIRECTOR, AN EXPANDED WORKFORCE WITH IMPROVED DIVERSITY, AND INCREASED RETENTION.  THE PURPOSE OF THE PROPOSED WORK UNDER STRATEGY A2 (FOUNDATIONAL CAPABILITIES) IS TO ADDRESS CRITICAL GAPS AND SUPPORT ACCREDITATION ACTIVITIES. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE UPDATED STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES, NEW ACCOUNTABILITY, NEW PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT MECHANISMS, IMPLEMENTATION OF CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT SYSTEMS, AND IMPROVED OPERATIONAL SYSTEMS.  THE PURPOSE OF THE PROPOSED WORK UNDER STRATEGY A3 (DATA MODERNIZATION) IS TO IMPROVE DATA SYSTEMS THAT WILL ALLOW RIDOH TO LEVERAGE DATA-DRIVEN, EMPIRICAL METHODS TO ADDRESS HEALTH DISPARITIES BY ASSESSING THE CURRENT SYSTEMS, AND UNDERTAKE IDENTIFIED OPPORTUNITIES FOR MODERNIZATION. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE A COMPLETED ASSESSMENT, AND ENHANCEMENTS IMPLEMENTED THAT INCREASE INTEROPERABILITY AND IMPROVE RIDOH’S ABILITY TO ADDRESS HEALTH DISPARITIES.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The purpose of the Emerging Infections Programs (EIP) is to assist in local, state, and national efforts to prevent, control, and monitor the public health impact of infectious diseases. The EIP cooperative agreement was formed in 1995 as a key component of CDC’s national strategy to address and reduce emerging infectious disease (EID) threats.  The EIP is a population-based network of state health agencies and their collaborators, including (but not limited to) academic institutions, local health departments, public health and clinical laboratories, infection control professionals, and healthcare providers.   The unique strength of the EIP lies in the network’s ability to quickly translate surveillance and research activities into informed policy and public health practice.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The intent of this program is to fund state, local, and territorial public health departments for HHS Secretarial declared and non-declared public health emergencies having an overwhelming impact on jurisdictional resources. These emergencies require federal support to effectively respond to, manage, and address a significant public health threat. CDC seeks to enhance the Nation’s ability to rapidly mobilize and respond to specific public health crises or emergencies. In addition to immediate response activities, this program provides a mechanism to accelerate readiness for an impending infectious disease threat or other public health crises identified on the event horizon.
